'''Michael H. Dickinson''' (born 1963) is an American fly [[bioengineer]] and [[neuroscientist]], and Zarem Professor of Biology and Bioengineering at the [[California Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bbe.caltech.edu/content/michael-h-dickinson|title=Michael H. Dickinson - www.bbe.caltech.edu|website=www.bbe.caltech.edu|access-date=2015-07-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180902010306/http://www.bbe.caltech.edu/content/michael-h-dickinson|archive-date=2018-09-02|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://dickinsonlab.caltech.edu/|title=Dickinson Lab|website=dickinsonlab.caltech.edu}}</ref> He studies ''[[Drosophila]]'' flight control systems and sensory processing and was dubbed the Fly Guy by The Scientist.<ref name="The Scientist profile">{{cite news |title=Fly Guy |url=https://www.the-scientist.com/fly-guy-40668 |work=The Scientist Magazine® |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Dickinson was born in [[Seaford, Delaware]], in 1963 but grew up in Baltimore before moving to Philadelphia.<ref name="Podcast Profile">{{cite news |title=627: Dr. Michael Dickinson: Sorting Out the Science of Fruit Fly Flight and Behavior |url=https://www.peoplebehindthescience.com/dr-michael-dickinson-2/ |work=People Behind the Science Podcast |date=18 October 2021}}</ref> He graduated from [[Brown University]] with a B.S. in 1984, and from [[University of Washington]] with a Ph.D. in 1989.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.icb.ucsb.edu/people/researchers_profile.php?ResearcherID=32 |title=ICB &#124; People |access-date=2010-04-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100625183723/http://www.icb.ucsb.edu/people/researchers_profile.php?ResearcherID=32 |archive-date=2010-06-25 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He did his postdoctoral work with [[Karl Georg Götz]] at the [[University of Tübingen]].<ref name="NYTime Profile">{{cite news |last1=Gorman |first1=James |title=Focusing on Fruit Flies, Curiosity Takes Flight |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/10/08/science/focusing-on-fruit-flies-curiosity-takes-flight.html |work=The New York Times |date=7 October 2013}}</ref>

==Career and Research==
He was an assistant professor at the [[University of Chicago]] in 1991,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uchospitals.edu/news/1995/19950000-how-flies-fly.html|title=How flies fly - UChicago Medicine|website=www.uchospitals.edu}}</ref> before moving to the [[University of California, Berkeley]], in 1996.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scienceblog.com/community/older/archives/G/ucb773.html|title=Science Blog -- Michael Dickinson Named MacArthur Fellow|website=www.scienceblog.com}}</ref> He was at [[California Institute of Technology]] from 2002 to 2011 before moving to the [[University of Washington]] from 2010 to 2014.<ref>{{cite web |title=Michael Dickinson {{!}} tedxcaltech.com |url=http://www.tedxcaltech.com/content/michael-dickinson.html |website=www.tedxcaltech.com}}</ref><ref name="NYTime Profile" /> He is now back at Caltech.

He is a Monitoring Editor at [[the Journal of Experimental Biology]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://jeb.biologists.org/site/about/editor_bios.xhtml |title=Editor biographies |access-date=2015-07-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150815234114/http://jeb.biologists.org/site/about/editor_bios.xhtml |archive-date=2015-08-15 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was a course director of the Neural Systems and Behavior course at the [[Marine Biological Laboratory]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sites.google.com/site/nsbmbl/ns-b-history|title=NS&B History - Neural Systems and Behavior @ MBL|website=sites.google.com}}</ref>

==Awards==
